paper.title: Top-$k$ Pareto Bandits: Hypervolume Regret for Multi-Objective Slate Selection

settings.name_in_paper: Top-k Pareto bandits (multi-objective slate selection, hypervolume alpha-regret)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Multi-objective (vector-valued) rewards; regret measured via dominated hypervolume of the selected slate.
unmapped: Each arm yields a d-dimensional reward vector in [0,1]^d with eta-sub-Gaussian coordinates
Slate reward is the dominated hypervolume HV(S) of the mean vectors w.r.t. a reference point r
Regret is (1-1/e)-approximation regret against the best size-k subset
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t\in[T]$, the agent selects a subset $S_t\subseteq[n]$ of size $|S_t|=k$ (a \emph{slate}) and observes the vectors $\{\mathbf{X}_{i,t}: i\in S_t\}$ (semi-bandit feedback). ... $\bar{r}_t = \alpha V^\star - \mathrm{HV}(S_t), \quad \bar{R}_T = \sum_{t=1}^{T} \bar{r}_t.$

symbols.C_d: coordinate-wise Lipschitz constant of the hypervolume, C_d <= d when rewards in [0,1]^d and r=0

conditions: each reward coordinate eta-sub-Gaussian and bounded in [0,1]
holds on the event E of valid confidence intervals, P(E) >= 1-delta
tuning: beta_i(t) = sqrt(2 eta log(n d t^2/delta)/N_i(t-1))

source.label: thm:gapfree
source.quote: Assume each reward coordinate is $\eta$-sub-Gaussian and bounded in $[0,1]$. On $\mathcal{E}$, \[ \bar{R}_T \;=\; O\!\left( C_d \sqrt{n k T \log T} \right). \]

results.notes: n arms mapped to K, slate size k mapped to m. Comparator is the best size-k subset (alpha=1-1/e approximation regret). Detailed version Theorem 4 (thm:gap-free) restates the same bound. Abstract states O~(d sqrt(nkT)) using C_d<=d.

symbols.Delta_greedy: minimum stage-wise gap of the true-mean greedy benchmark G*: min over stages l and arms i != i*_l of Delta(i*_l|G*_{l-1}) - Delta(i|G*_{l-1})

conditions: each reward coordinate eta-sub-Gaussian and bounded in [0,1]
greedy maximizer of G* unique at every stage
safe-pruning step never eliminates an arm of G* (assumed, not proved)
holds on the event E, P(E) >= 1-delta
tuning: beta_i(t) = sqrt(2 eta log(n d t^2/delta)/N_i(t-1))

source.label: thm:gapdep
source.quote: Under the same assumptions, if the greedy maximizer of $G^\star$ is unique at every stage and the safe-pruning step never eliminates an arm of $G^\star$, then on $\mathcal{E}$, \[ \bar{R}_T \;=\; O\!\left( \frac{n k^{2.5} \log T}{\Delta_{\min}} \right). \]

results.notes: Detailed version Theorem 5 (thm:gap-dependent) restates it. Delta_min is a greedy-stage gap, not an arm gap, so renamed.

bound.expression_latex: \mathbb{E}[\bar{R}_T] \leq \min\{ O(\sqrt{n k T \log T}), O(\frac{n k^{2.5} \log T}{\Delta_{\min}}) \} + O(1)

conditions: each reward coordinate eta-sub-Gaussian and bounded in [0,1]

source.label: thm:combined
source.quote: With $\delta = 1/T$, \[ \mathbb{E}\big[\bar{R}_T\big] \leq \min\Bigl\{ O\left(\sqrt{n k T \log T}\right), O\left(\frac{n k^{2.5} \log T}{\Delta_{\min}}\right) \Bigr\} + O(1). \] In particular $\mathbb{E}[\bar{R}_T]/T \to 0$

results.notes: Gap-free branch of the min. C_d dropped in this statement as written (absorbed in O for fixed d). Detailed version Theorem 8 (thm:main) identical.
